blocks.content: The pattern of change in allele frequency shown in Figure 3.4 is very nearly that expected theoretically for an ideal population, as shown in [[see_figure:3.5]]. This distribution was obtained by successive multiplication of a matrix whose elements are given by the transition probabilities in Equation 3.2. Although the full-blown theory of random genetic drift requires mathematics beyond the scope of this book <sup>[140,181,337,339,342,352,787]</sup>, in the next section we provide an introductory tidbit to impart the flavor. If you are a student with no background in calculus, the discussion may seem quite mysterious, but please do not be discouraged because a detailed understanding is not necessary to understand the rest of this chapter or anything later in the book.
